prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park is likely to prevail on its declaratory-judgment counterclaim that the lease remained in force (NCO vacated despite the landlord's notice that termination conditions were unmet) and to recover substantial unpaid rent through the original lease term, subject to a mitigation offset; NCO's fraud, unjust enrichment, and overcharge claims face significant doctrinal hurdles given the fully-integrated, negotiated commercial lease. Fee-shifting and default-rate interest under Section 14.04 add meaningful additional recovery beyond the base rent-stream figure.

issues.label: Validity of NCO's early termination exercise
Counterclaim for declaratory judgment that lease is ongoing
Past-due and continuing rent (core damages claim)
Landlord's duty to mitigate / re-letting offset
NCO's rent-overcharge / square-footage claim (as affecting rent calc and termination conditions)
Fee-shifting recovery (attorneys' fees and costs) under Section 14.04
Default-rate interest on unpaid rent and fees

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
